title: Sun Bin Reduces the Campfires
text:
Years after his rival Pang Juan had him mutilated, Sun Bin faced him again. In about 342 BC the state of Wei attacked Han, and Qi sent an army under Tian Ji with Sun Bin as strategist. As before, they marched toward the Wei capital, and Pang Juan turned back to chase them.

According to Sima Qian, Sun Bin knew the Wei soldiers despised the men of Qi as cowards. He ordered that on the first night the camp should show cooking fires for a hundred thousand men, on the second for fifty thousand, and on the third for thirty thousand. Pang Juan counted the fire pits and concluded that Qi's troops were deserting in droves. He left his infantry behind and raced ahead with light troops.

Sun Bin calculated where Pang Juan would arrive at nightfall: Maling, where the road ran through a narrow pass. He had a large tree stripped of bark and wrote on the bare wood that Pang Juan would die under this tree. He hid ten thousand crossbowmen along the road with orders to shoot when they saw a light.

Pang Juan arrived in the dark, saw writing on the tree and lit a torch to read it. The crossbows fired at once, his army broke, and Pang Juan cut his own throat. Qi destroyed the Wei army and captured the Wei crown prince.
lesson: People read evidence through what they already believe. Give a confident opponent the signs he expects to see and he may rush into the place you have prepared.
people: Sun Bin, Pang Juan, Tian Ji
source: Sima Qian, Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji), chapter 65
caveat: The exact year and site of Maling are debated, and the details of the inscribed tree may be embellished.
